audit.title: Selecting Quality Data Feeds

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Category sections lead well — "These are data feeds that follow a standardized data feeds workflow to report market prices." The opening intro paragraph is diffuse (liability framing before any definition); implied question "how do I pick a feed?" isn't answered in the first sentence.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; no action needed. 1 H1, max depth H4, 0 level skips, 0 sections over 600 words — near-ideal RAG chunk boundaries.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Market-hours table and the `$1.05` bound example are excellent. Weakened by vague quantifiers flagged in the facts ("several," "various," "significant," "wide range") in the risk-factor bullets where a range or threshold would be more liftable.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Reasonable external links (Aave CAPO proposal, Wikipedia corporate-action/soak-testing, blog.chain.link) but the facts show **0 links to primary sources** and 2 opaque anchors ("here," "this").

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Good self-contained definitions for "Bounded Market Price Feeds," "Exchange rate feeds," and single-source feeds. The eight risk categories lack a one-line canonical definition each in a scannable form.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak per facts — 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical missing, no `dateModified`. A risk/policy page especially benefits from a visible last-updated signal. `<head>` could not be verified from the `.md` endpoint.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No fenced blocks. Largely acceptable for a conceptual page, but the shutdown-behavior facts (`latestAnswer` → `0`, `latestRoundData` reverts) would benefit from a minimal tagged snippet.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Broad lifecycle coverage (categories → hours → mitigation → wrapped assets → front-running). Missing symptom-phrased entry points ("why does my feed return 0?", "feed reverts with no data").

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; consistent capitalized entity naming ("Market Pricing Risk," "Data Feed") aids entity resolution.

audit.summary: This is a well-structured conceptual page defining Chainlink's data-feed risk categories, market hours, and integration risk-mitigation practices. Its biggest GEO strength is clean chunking — 32 sections, median 150 words, no level skips, and a dense, concrete market-hours table that is highly liftable. Its biggest opportunity is that the eight-category risk taxonomy lives entirely in prose: a single comparison table mapping category → risk level → deprecation eligibility would give engines the structured "reasons" they cite. Metadata is the mechanical weak spot (no JSON-LD, no canonical, no dates), though the `.md` endpoint likely strips the `<head>` — verify against the HTML page before treating as absent.

recommendations.title: Add a risk-category comparison table
recommendations.where: top of `## Data Feed Categories`, above the bullet list
recommendations.issue: eight categories are defined only in separate prose sections; no single extractable unit
recommendations.change: add a table with columns Category | Risk level | Definition (one line) | Deprecation-eligible? | e.g. `🟢 Low | Lowest | Standardized workflow, multiple sources aggregated | No`. Lead each cell with the canonical fact.
recommendations.why: engines cite tables to build justified "which feed should I use" answers; this is the page's highest-lift single change.

recommendations.title: Add symptom-phrased subheadings for feed-failure behavior
recommendations.where: `#### Data Feed Shutdown Policy` NOTE block
recommendations.issue: answer buried under a policy heading — "calls to the feed will behave as follows"
recommendations.change: add an H3/H4 phrased as the query, e.g. `### Why does my feed return 0 / latestRoundData revert?` with the two bullets as the answer-first body.
recommendations.why: devs/agents query the error symptom, not "shutdown policy"; concept-titled prose loses this retrieval even though the answer is present verbatim.

recommendations.title: Add TechArticle JSON-LD, canonical, and visible last-updated
recommendations.issue: facts report 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical missing, no `dateModified`
recommendations.change: emit `TechArticle` schema with `dateModified` and a `canonical` to the non-`.md` URL; surface a visible "Last updated" line. Verify the HTML `<head>` first — the `.md` endpoint may already strip existing tags.
recommendations.why: freshness and schema raise agent trust (E-E-A-T) for a policy page where currency matters.

recommendations.title: Replace opaque anchor text
recommendations.where: `### Unknown and Known Users` ("you can do so [here]") and the ETF/Forex NOTE ("contact us [here]")
recommendations.change: relabel to describe the target, e.g. "[submit your contact information](…)".
recommendations.why: descriptive anchors improve link-context extraction and citation attribution.

recommendations.title: Tighten the intro to be answer-first
recommendations.issue: opens with "consider the quality of the data … Ultimately you are responsible…" before defining anything
recommendations.change: lead with a one-sentence canonical statement: "Chainlink groups data feeds into eight market-pricing-risk categories (Low → Very High, plus New Token, Custom, Deprecating, Unrated) to signal intended use and data-quality risk."
recommendations.why: the first liftable sentence should answer "how are feeds categorized?" and resist parametric priors.

recommendations.title: Add a minimal tagged code snippet for shutdown behavior
recommendations.issue: API behavior described in inline prose only
recommendations.change: add a short `solidity`-tagged block showing `latestAnswer()` returning `0` and `latestRoundData()` reverting, with a one-line comment.
recommendations.why: copy-pasteable, language-tagged snippets are preferentially extracted by coding agents.

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifiers with ranges where feasible
recommendations.where: Medium/Very High risk-factor bullets ("Lower or inconsistent asset volume," "extremely low levels")
recommendations.change: where a defined threshold exists, state it (e.g. probationary-period length for New Token feeds, notification lead time — "two weeks" is already good, extend that pattern).
recommendations.why: quantitative specifics are among the highest-lift changes for citation.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifiers flagged in facts ("many, several, various, some, most, wide range, significant, fast") — acceptable in a risk-narrative page but reducible in the risk-factor bullets.
No dated/freshness signal on a page whose content (deprecation policy, category assignments) is time-sensitive.
No keyword stuffing, no marketing fluff, no unresolved cross-references — clean.
offPageNotes: The `.md` endpoint appears to serve body only; pass the raw HTML `<head>` through the CLI so schema/canonical/date presence can be confirmed rather than inferred absent.
`llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good site-level discoverability signal.
Category assignments for individual feeds live on other pages (`data.chain.link`); internal links from those feed pages back into this canonical taxonomy would reinforce the hub pattern.
